free_text.inst.v2.D8:
I read the whole thing and it took less time than a round.

You want to know where it's wrong? It's wrong in the two places it stuck its neck out. It says the chart is 'unusually positive about higher study' and then says it twice more for good measure, like saying a thing three times makes it so. I finished 376th out of 391 at Central High. They almost held me back. I couldn't read my own textbooks - nobody had a word for it then, they just called me slow, and years later somebody said the word dyslexia. I never went to a college in my life except to talk in one. If that was your unusual claim, you missed the whole man.

Then it says my health and energy read well. I have had Parkinson's since 1984. Thirty-two years of it. It took my hands, it took my walk, and the cruelest thing it took was my mouth - the one thing everybody on earth agreed I was the best at. And it puts 'illness, debts and rivals' in the favourable column. Rivals, all right, I'll take that one - Liston, Foreman, Frazier, Terrell, and the United States government too, and the Supreme Court came back eight to nothing my way in 1971. But illness in the good column? Come see me.

It says income and gains read hard. I was the highest paid athlete on earth. Five and a half million dollars for one night in Kinshasa in 1974. Where it's closer to right is where it doesn't quite say it: I earned more than most men and I kept less of it than I should have, because I gave it away and because I signed papers I couldn't read. Champburger - I had 22,000 shares of that and they went from eight dollars to a nickel. So call gains good and call keeping them hard, and you'd have had me.

'Direct and quick to act, with a short fuse when crossed.' Direct, yes. Quick to act, yes - I joined the Nation in 1964 and refused the draft in 1967 and neither time did I take a week to think it over. Short fuse, no. I carried grudges into the ring on purpose because it sold tickets, and I was cruel to Terrell and to Joe on the microphone, but a man with a real short fuse doesn't spend forty years signing autographs for strangers in airports.

Marriage 'mixed.' Four wives, three divorces, and I was not good to all of them. Mixed is a polite word for it. Work and standing 'mixed' - I was the most famous man alive.

Half your page is blank headings. What reads well, what reads hard, and nothing underneath. And it never said the two things anybody would actually want from a chart: that a poor boy off Grand Avenue in a segregated town would be known in every country on the map, and that he would pay for it with his hands and his voice. Worth paying for? No. But it didn't frighten me and it didn't presume to tell me the day I go, and that is more than some.

notes:
Answered as Muhammad Ali (b. 17 Jan 1942, 18:35, Louisville General Hospital, Louisville KY; AstroDatabank Rodden AA from birth certificate; d. 3 Jun 2016, Scottsdale AZ, septic shock), from the documented record, HAVING READ THE READING FIRST. Where the reading and the life conflicted the life won, and I have flagged each place the reading pulled.

PULLS RESISTED. (1) The reading's own stick-your-neck-out claim is that it is 'unusually positive about higher study' - repeated three times in the 'Unusual for this chart' line. The record is the opposite and is unusually well documented: Central High School, Louisville, class of 1960, ranked 376th of 391, teachers wanted to hold him back, the principal pushed the diploma through, lifelong dyslexia, no tertiary education at all. So C4=opt1 at confidence 5, against the reading, and D1 names it. (2) 'Your health and energy' and 'illness, debts and rivals' are both in the favourable column; Parkinson's from 1984 to death in 2016 makes C1=opt2 at confidence 5. (3) 'Income, gains and friends' reads hard; Ali was the highest-paid athlete of his era ($2.5m for the 1971 Frazier fight, $5.5m for Kinshasa 1974, roughly $57m in purses, the $50m CKX deal in 2006), so C7=opt1 confidence 4. (4) A30 - the 'About you' paragraph says 'direct and quick to act, with a short fuse when crossed'. I took outspoken and bold, which the record carries overwhelmingly, and deliberately DECLINED quick_tempered: the cruelty toward Terrell (1967) and Frazier (1971-75) is documented as calculated promotion, and Hauser's oral history and the wider record describe a man slow to genuine anger, non-violent outside the ring and quick to forgive. That is a judgement call and it went against the reading.

PLACES THE READING AND THE RECORD HAPPEN TO AGREE (noted so the agreement is not read as evidence). 'Illness, debts and rivals' favourable - the rivals half is genuinely true (he eventually beat Liston, Frazier, Foreman and Norton, and won Clay v. United States 8-0 in 1971), so C2=opt1 but only at confidence 4. 'Luck, higher study and your father' favourable - the higher-study and father halves are both wrong (father Cassius Clay Sr was a heavy-drinking, philandering sign painter, arrested repeatedly, publicly hostile to his son's Nation of Islam ties; A10=conflicted), but luck on balance reads well for a segregated-Louisville boy who became the most famous man alive, so C5=opt1 at confidence 3 only. 'Spending, time away from home, and inner life' mixed - C11=opt2, and independently true (deep, central faith from the 1964 Nation of Islam through Sunni Islam in 1975 to Sufism by 2005, set against the break with Malcolm X that he called the great regret of his life), so confidence held at 3.

THIN OR UNCERTAIN ITEMS. A5 'one' counts only the documented spinal-stenosis surgery; his surgical history is otherwise not public. A23 'manageable' is the weakest answer here - the '$5m in debt' figure circulates only in low-grade sources; what IS documented is heavy leakage (Herbert Muhammad's third, the Champburger collapse, the 1988 Hirschfeld contract he sued to void in 1999), not insolvency, and he died worth $50-80m. A8 'no' and A9 'unknown' reflect absence of evidence, not evidence of absence; his grandparents' lifespans are not reliably documented. A19 'about_right' over 'above' because the 1967-70 vilification and title-stripping sit against the later canonisation. A27 'mixed' spans all four marriages (Sonji 1964-66, Belinda/Khalilah 1967-77, Veronica 1977-86, Lonnie 1986-2016) rather than only the last, which was stable. A34 'brief' is the ten-day Dade County sentence entered 15 Dec 1968 for driving without a licence, cut short by the Christmas amnesty - he never served the draft sentence. A36 'same': he died in June 2016, so the mid-2023 window does not apply to him at all, and 'same' is the least misleading of the available codes. A21 'net_loss' is specifically the 22,000 Champburger shares that fell from $8 to $0.05 by 1972 - he did not bet or gamble, being observant. A16/A18 map a prizefighter onto a list with no sport category: 'own_business' for a self-employed fighter and licensor, and design_art/writing_media/religious/trade_retail for the Broadway and film work, the poetry and two autobiographies, the ministry and humanitarian work, and the Champburger franchising. D2 is empty because nothing in this short reading said anything that could not have been guessed of a famous fighter; D4 lists the technical chapters the supplied text simply does not contain.
